analysis: Integration of 5 unit analyses. The PR is docs/changelog plus SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift (T-041, TB-007, A-001). Hosts with >=96 GiB RAM now default complete-checkpoint SSD staging to 3 GiB / 2500 ms, up from 1 GiB / 1000 ms. SSDHybridCheckpointStoreFactory.swift wires the new defaults in. Explicit DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_MAX_STAGE_MB/_MS still win, invalid values fall back to the defaults, and attention-block caches keep the old defaults. The ModelCheckpointStorageArtifacts.swift change is test-only. The at-rest posture in T-041 (a)-(d) is unchanged: AES-GCM/DBK3, HMAC lookup tags, the 1800 s TTL, scope salting, the disk budget and the write cap are untouched. Posture (e) (no persistent carve, transient staging reserved via GlobalKVCacheBudget) is documented as preserved. Only the transient staging size grows. Larger restorable prefixes (about 16k tokens vs 8k) marginally extend the same-account TTFT oracle (SEC-035), which is already accepted in kind. No concrete regression was found. Coverage limits: the production callers, the GlobalKVCacheBudget implementation, the write-behind queue cap (max(512 MiB, maxStageBytes + slack)) and the read maximumPlaintextBytes bound were not supplied. A later pass should verify that reservation happens before allocation and fails closed under memory pressure, that the 3 GiB stage cannot starve live serving (T-010/T-029 class), and that the explicit env override precedence holds. T-041's detection_hint does not list staging caps as a sign-off trigger. No threat-model update is needed.
